name: Richard Pascoe
story: In 1990 Richard Pascoe and John Penny published work on the interchange of data between geographic information systems and on constructing interfaces for geographic-data exchange.

In 2001 Bryan Clarke represented Christchurch as the local-government Data Modeller on the Crown emergency-services core-data project, working with University of Canterbury’s Richard Pascoe, who advised on UML and ISO/TC211 standards.

Pascoe's 1989 University of Canterbury MSc thesis, Translating Data Between Geographic Information Systems, studied conversion between otherwise incompatible GIS data formats. It proposed a decoder, a relational intermediate representation and an encoder to support transfer. This documents a New Zealand academic contribution to geospatial data interchange before routine adoption of later open standards; the thesis alone does not establish subsequent commercial deployment.
